install_point: after all Stage-A initialization, immediately before workload exec (never before no_new_privs)
change_control: docs/seccomp-derivation/policy.md section 5: NO UNDOCUMENTED SYSCALL EXPANSION. Any change requires an explicit diff, a documented reason, a security-impact assessment, relevant test changes, and a docs/ADR update. check_trace_regression.py fails any observed syscall outside this list.

changelog.reason: Native Phase C verification on Ubuntu 24.04 / kernel 6.8 / x86_64: git 2.43.0 (ADR-005 toolchain) requires chdir for the closed-set operations (status/diff/ls-files/merge-base/rev-parse) - the -C worktree handling and work-tree-top resolution.
changelog.security_impact: chdir is a cwd-only syscall (same class as the already-allowed getcwd): no privilege gain, no namespace/network/filesystem-boundary escape.

changelog.syscall: socket, connect, sendto, recvfrom, getsockopt, setsockopt, getsockname, getpeername
changelog.reason: v0.2 networking prerequisites: minimum syscall set for sandbox-to-proxy loopback communication.
changelog.security_impact: Network syscalls in isolation do not grant network access; the network namespace (no interfaces, loopback down) and seccomp are independent layers.

changelog.syscall: chmod, close_range, copy_file_range, fadvise64, fstatfs, lgetxattr, link, listxattr, rename, statfs, statx, symlink, umask, uname, unlinkat
changelog.reason: Native Ubuntu 24.04 / kernel 6.8 / x86_64 trace of the complete workload set (t0_sh_echo, t0_sh_exit, t1_sh_fileops, t1_python_hello, t1_python_agentish, t1_git_basics, t1_git_closedset) observed 63 unique syscalls. 15 syscalls not in the 54-syscall allowlist were identified. All 15 are legitimate toolchain operations: glibc runtime (close_range, fadvise64, statx), coreutils (copy_file_range, fstatfs, lgetxattr, listxattr, statfs, umask, uname, unlinkat), and git (chmod, link, rename, symlink). All are tier1. None enables privilege escalation, namespace escape, capability changes, network access, or sandbox escape.
changelog.security_impact: All 15 are filesystem/metadata operations confined to the mount namespace. chmod/link/symlink/rename operate only on workload-created files within the sandbox. clone/clone3 remain denied. Network namespace remains deny-by-construction.
changelog.evidence: Native trace on Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-137-generic x86_64, Python 3.12.3, strace 6.8. 63 unique syscalls observed; 15 identified as missing from the 54-syscall allowlist via check_trace_regression.py.

changelog.reason: Phase 10 (v0.2 Step 4) dependency-installation workflow: native measurement of pip install (networked through the validating CONNECT proxy, Debian 13 container, Python 3.11, pip 24.x, strace 6.13) under the real 69-syscall filter showed exactly one genuinely required missing syscall. pip's adjacent_tmp_file (pip/_internal/utils/filesystem.py) calls os.fsync on the downloaded wheel before the atomic rename - the install aborts with PermissionError when fsync is EPERM'd. The other five candidate syscalls observed in the raw trace (bind - urllib3 IPv6-availability probe, connection.py:139; clock_nanosleep - asyncio loop sleep; mremap - glibc malloc growth; readlinkat - dynamic-loader /proc/self/exe resolution; rmdir - pip temp-dir cleanup) are all attempted but tolerated: under a real default-deny EPERM filter pip installs successfully with all five denied. clone/clone3 are NOT used by pip (thread count 0) and remain denied.
changelog.security_impact: fsync is a durability-only syscall (flush file data to stable storage): it grants no privilege, no capability, no namespace/network/filesystem-boundary escape, and no information disclosure. It operates only on file descriptors the workload already holds (workload-created files in the writable layer). The socket-domain filter is unaffected. clone/clone3, bind, mremap, readlinkat, rmdir, clock_nanosleep remain denied - evidence: native real-seccomp test, 2026-08-23.
changelog.evidence: tools/seccomp-derivation/trace-results.json t1_pip_install (successful surface under the 70-syscall filter, strace 6.13, Debian 13 / Python 3.11 / pip 24.x, 2026-08-23). Necessity isolation: real seccomp default-deny EPERM filter (no_new_privs + PR_SET_SECCOMP), not LD_PRELOAD (which cannot intercept glibc-internal calls).

limitations: Native x86_64 trace-verified (Ubuntu 24.04 / kernel 6.8). aarch64 mappings derived from asm-generic/unistd.h and require native aarch64 trace verification. Threads (clone) denied by design. glibc/x86_64-specific syscalls may differ on other Linux distributions.
